title: Optimal central limit theorem for bounded random variables in high dimensions
summary: Let $W=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$, where the $X_i$ are independent centered random vectors in ${\mathbb R}^p$ with $|X_{ij}|\le B$ almost surely. Suppose that $\text{Cov}(W)$ has unit diagonal and smallest eigenvalue at least $b^2>0$. We prove that the distance between $W$ and a Gaussian vector with the same covariance, uniformly over axis-aligned rectangles, is at most $C\min\{1,b^{-2}Bn^{-1/2}\log^{3/2}(ep)\}$.
